AN ACT to amend the surrogate's court procedure act, in relation to

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2815

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the surrogate's court procedure act, in relation to
establishing new fee rates for large estates

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would amend the filing fee schedule for the value of estates,
ranging from estates less than $10,000 to estates that are worth
$5,000,000 and over.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Subdivision 7 of the section 2402 of the Surrogate's
Court procedure act by adding more brackets to the filing fee schedule
for estates, capping at $5,000,000.

Section 2: The effective date of this bill.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under current law, the filing fee rate charged to estates by the surro-
gate court is determine by a fee schedule, which caps at $1,250 for all
estates over $500,000. This cap is far too low and treats, for purposes
of charging fees, estates worth $500,000 the same as those worth
$50,000,000. This bill seeks to the make the fee schedule more progres-
sive by adding several new brackets past the original cap, including a
new filing fee cap of $10,000 for estates worth $5,000,000 and over.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.4952 of 2019-20; Referred to Judiciary

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Increased revenue for surrogates courts through new higher fee brackets
in the fee schedule.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law and shall apply to actions and proceedings commenced on or
after such effective date.

summary: Relates to establishing new fee rates for large estates; raises the fee rate for estates with a value over $5,000,000 to $10,000.
